title: Charging sessions
description: One record per charging session, built from vehicle.charging.events.v1. All derivations are in event time and use inputs only: deduplicate by event_id first, ignore arrival order, never read a processing-time clock. Input lateness is at most 300 seconds, so jobs must allow at least 300 seconds of lateness and drop nothing. Session boundaries, per VIN, ordering non-heartbeat and heartbeat charging events by event_time: a session starts at a charge_start and contains the following charge_progress/charge_stop events. It closes with close_reason = charge_stop at the first charge_stop. It closes with close_reason = gap_timeout when the next event for that VIN on the topic (any event_type, including heartbeat or a new charge_start) has event_time more than 30 minutes (1800000 ms) after the session's last event. Events outside a session are ignored. session_id = UUIDv5(namespace f5179d15-0fd7-5b5f-bf53-0852eb22d3d5, name = vin + '|' + event_id of the charge_start), with the event_id in lowercase canonical form and the name encoded as UTF-8 (RFC 9562 section 5.5). The namespace is UUIDv5(NAMESPACE_DNS, 'contracts.telemetry.example'). Field rules: connector_type, charger_type, charger_lat, charger_lon and start_soc_pct come from the charge_start; start_time is its event_time; end_time is the event_time of the session's last event (for gap_timeout this is the last event, not the last event + 30 minutes); energy_added_kwh and end_soc_pct come from the last event; peak_power_kw is the max power_kw over the session; event_count is the number of distinct event_ids in the session, including charge_start and charge_stop.

session_id.description: UUIDv5 over vin|charge_start event_id; see the schema description.
